root_cause.text: In the IPv6 TCP accept path, `tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()` initialized the v6-mapped child socket only after calling `tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()`, but that helper makes the child visible via the TCP ehash first, creating a race where other CPUs can access `newinet->pinet6` while it still points to the listener’s `ipv6_pinfo`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the v6-mapped child setup into a new `tcp_v6_mapped_child_init()` helper and has `tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()` invoke it before ehash insertion; the commit message explicitly says the post-`tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()` code was “done too late” because “the child socket is already visible from TCP ehash table,” and “newinet->pinet6 is still pointing to the listener ipv6_pinfo.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend the inet connection socket AF operations callback interface with an optional child-socket initialization hook.
intent_record.what: The function pointer type in `struct inet_connection_sock_af_ops` was changed to add a new trailing parameter: `void (*opt_child_init)(struct sock *newsk, const struct sock *sk)`. The existing parameters and return type remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: Any caller of this callback can now supply an optional child-socket initialization hook that will be invoked during request/socket handling. This extends the callback interface to support additional per-child setup behavior without changing the existing arguments.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() to accept an optional child socket initialization callback.
intent_record.what: The declaration of tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() was extended with a new trailing function pointer parameter, opt_child_init, which takes a new socket and the parent socket; the rest of the prototype remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, callers of tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() can now supply an optional child-socket initialization callback that will be invoked for the newly created socket, allowing protocol-specific post-accept setup to be performed during TCP SYN receive handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the `syn_recv_sock` call to match the extended function signature by supplying a trailing `NULL` argument.
intent_record.what: The call to `icsk->icsk_af_ops->syn_recv_sock()` in `tcp_get_cookie_sock()` was changed from passing six arguments to passing seven, adding a final `NULL` argument after `&own_req`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this updates the `syn_recv_sock` invocation to match an interface that now accepts an additional parameter, while still passing no extra data for that new slot. This allows the TCP child socket creation path to compile and call the address-family-specific hook with the expected signature.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the TCP fast open child socket creation call to match the revised `syn_recv_sock` callback signature.
intent_record.what: The call to `inet_csk(sk)->icsk_af_ops->syn_recv_sock(...)` was updated to pass one additional final argument, changing the argument list from six parameters to seven by appending `NULL` at the end.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes `tcp_fastopen_create_child()` invoke the `syn_recv_sock` callback with the updated function signature expected by the interface. It ensures the child socket creation path passes the extra context/parameter slot as null, preventing an argument mismatch and allowing the call to work correctly with the newer callback prototype.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock to accept an optional child-socket initialization callback.
intent_record.what: The function prototype of tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock was changed to add a new parameter: a callback named opt_child_init, with type void (*)(struct sock *newsk, const struct sock *sk).
intent_record.how: At runtime, callers can now pass an optional child-socket initialization function into tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock, allowing additional initialization logic to be applied to the newly created child socket during TCP SYN reception processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Invoke opt_child_init for newly accepted TCP sockets when available so child socket state is initialized correctly in IPv6-enabled builds.
intent_record.what: In tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock(), after sk_setup_caps(newsk, dst) and before tcp_ca_openreq_child(newsk, dst), the code now conditionally calls opt_child_init(newsk, sk) inside an #if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6) block when opt_child_init is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this initializes child socket options for the newly created TCP socket when the callback is available, but only in builds with IPv6 enabled. This allows inherited per-socket options or IPv6-related child state to be set up during SYN receive handling instead of being skipped.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the TCP request socket child creation call to match the new `syn_recv_sock()` signature by passing a NULL final argument.
intent_record.what: The call to `inet_csk(sk)->icsk_af_ops->syn_recv_sock()` in `tcp_check_req()` was changed to pass one additional argument: `NULL` is now supplied as the final parameter, updating the function call from six arguments to seven.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the way the SYN-received child socket is created by matching the updated `syn_recv_sock()` interface. It prevents argument mismatch and ensures the function receives an explicit null value for the new parameter, which can affect child socket setup behavior inside the protocol implementation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add dedicated initialization for IPv6-mapped TCP child sockets and extend SYN-recv setup with a child init callback.
intent_record.what: Added a new helper function `tcp_v6_mapped_child_init(struct sock *newsk, const struct sock *sk)` that initializes IPv6 state for v6-mapped TCP child sockets, including copying `ipv6_pinfo`, setting the source address, AF ops, backlog receiver, MD5/AO-specific ops, multicast-related fields, and flow info. Also changed `tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()` to accept an additional callback parameter `opt_child_init` of type `void (*)(struct sock *newsk, const struct sock *sk)`.
intent_record.how: This enables specialized initialization of IPv6-mapped child sockets during TCP receive-socket creation, ensuring the child inherits and adjusts the correct IPv6/MPTCP/security/multicast state instead of relying on generic setup alone. The new callback hook also allows the caller to supply child-specific option initialization logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor the IPv4-mapped child socket path in tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() to delegate initialization to tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() via a dedicated callback.
intent_record.what: The IPv4 fast path inside tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() was removed, including all of the post-creation IPv6-mapped socket setup that used to be performed inline. In its place, the ETH_P_IP branch now immediately returns the result of tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock(), passing an additional callback argument tcp_v6_mapped_child_init.
intent_record.how: For IPv4 packets received on the IPv6 listening socket path, child socket creation is now delegated to tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() with a dedicated initialization hook. This preserves the mapped-IPv6 child setup behavior while moving the special-case initialization out of tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock(), reducing duplication and centralizing the IPv4 child socket setup logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend `subflow_syn_recv_sock()` to accept a child socket initialization callback for additional per-socket setup.
intent_record.what: The function `subflow_syn_recv_sock()` has been updated to take an additional argument: a function pointer `opt_child_init` with signature `void (*opt_child_init)(struct sock *newsk, const struct sock *sk)`. The existing parameters and body shown in the hunk are otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change allows the caller to pass an optional child-socket initialization callback into `subflow_syn_recv_sock()`, enabling extra setup logic to run for the newly created socket during SYN-RECV handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass `opt_child_init` to child socket creation so the new socket is initialized with the required option data.
intent_record.what: The call to `listener->icsk_af_ops->syn_recv_sock(...)` in `subflow_syn_recv_sock()` was updated to pass an additional argument, `opt_child_init`, changing the function invocation from six to seven parameters.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the child socket creation path now forwards `opt_child_init` into the lower-level `syn_recv_sock` implementation, allowing that code to use the extra option data during child socket initialization. This can alter how the new socket is initialized and enables behavior that was previously unavailable.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend `smc_tcp_syn_recv_sock` to accept an optional child-socket initialization callback.
intent_record.what: The function `smc_tcp_syn_recv_sock` had its parameter list extended by adding a new callback argument: `void (*opt_child_init)(struct sock *newsk, const struct sock *sk)`. The existing parameters were left unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, callers can now pass an optional child-socket initialization function into `smc_tcp_syn_recv_sock`, allowing additional setup to be performed on the newly created socket during SYN-received handling. This enables more flexible initialization of the child socket without changing the core function body shown in the diff.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass `opt_child_init` through to the underlying `syn_recv_sock` call so child socket initialization uses the correct state.
intent_record.what: The call to `smc->ori_af_ops->syn_recv_sock(...)` was updated to pass an additional argument, `opt_child_init`, as a new final parameter in the argument list.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the original address-family `syn_recv_sock` implementation now receives the child-initialization option/state, allowing it to initialize the newly created child socket with that extra context; this changes how the child socket is set up during TCP/SMC handshake completion.

Pass `opt_child_init` through to the underlying `syn_recv_sock` call so child socket initialization uses the correct state.

consistency_review.core_intent: Extend TCP SYN-receive child socket creation paths and related AF operation callbacks to optionally invoke a child-socket initialization hook.
Update TCP child socket creation calls to conform to an extended syn_recv_sock signature, including passing child initialization state.
consistency_review.reason: Most hunks are about plumbing opt_child_init or a trailing NULL through syn_recv_sock call sites to match the new signature, while hunk 7 introduces a separate IPv6-mapped socket initialization change and broader setup logic that is not part of the same narrow signature-plumbing fix.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add child-socket initialization hooks for TCP, including IPv6-mapped and SYN-recv paths, so newly created sockets are initialized correctly.
Extend TCP/AF connection socket receive-SYN child socket creation paths to support an optional child-socket initialization callback.
Propagate the new child-socket initialization argument through `syn_recv_sock`-based call sites so they match the updated callback signature.
Initialize newly created TCP child sockets correctly in IPv6-enabled paths by adding or invoking child socket initialization hooks.

relevance_review.reason: The changes add an optional child-socket initialization callback to TCP/AF accept paths, but they do not specifically fix the IPv6 race where `newinet->pinet6` is left pointing at the listener’s `ipv6_pinfo` before the child becomes visible in the ehash. There is no indication these hunks move IPv6 initialization before publication or otherwise address the race condition described in the root cause.

The root cause is a race from child-socket initialization happening too late in the IPv6 TCP accept path. This group explicitly propagates a new child-initialization argument through syn_recv_sock call sites and passes opt_child_init/NULL so the child socket is initialized during creation rather than afterward, which directly matches the vulnerability fix direction.

The change directly targets the race in the IPv6 TCP accept path by initializing IPv6-mapped child sockets earlier via child-init hooks. This matches the root cause where child visibility occurred before `newinet->pinet6` was properly initialized.

The change targets tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() in the IPv4-mapped child socket path, which is exactly where the race occurred. Refactoring initialization to be delegated through tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() is directly related to the ordering/visibility issue around child socket setup.

candidates.rationale: This call creates the child socket via the IPv4 helper before the IPv6-specific fields are initialized, matching the race described in the root cause where the child becomes visible while newinet->pinet6 still points to the listener's ipv6_pinfo.

This completes the vulnerable tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() invocation that returns a child socket before tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() copies/rewires the IPv6 state, enabling early exposure of an incompletely initialized v6-mapped child.
This initialization happens after the helper call, so it is too late to prevent other CPUs from observing the child via the ehash with an incorrect pinet6 pointer inherited from the listener.
The IPv6 control block is copied only after the child is already created and potentially visible, which is the core race that leaves the new socket temporarily backed by the listener's ipv6_pinfo.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call creates the child socket through the IPv4 helper before the IPv6-specific state is initialized, allowing the child to become visible in the TCP ehash while still carrying the listener's IPv6 pointer.
This completes the vulnerable tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() invocation that returns a child socket before tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() fixes up the IPv6 fields, enabling the race window.
This assignment happens only after the child has already been created by the helper, so other CPUs may observe the socket before pinet6 is corrected.
The IPv6 control block is copied after the child socket is created, which is too late to prevent exposure of an incompletely initialized v6-mapped child.
